chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson connects growing Christlike qualities with developing our divine nature. How does growth in love prevent received knowledge from remaining idle?
chapters.1.summary: Simon Peter writes to those who share the same precious faith. God’s power has given them all they need for life and godliness. Through his promises they share in the divine nature. They are to add goodness, knowledge, self-control, endurance, godliness, affection, and love to faith. With these they will not be idle or unfruitful. Peter says he will soon put off his tent and wants them to remember. He was an eyewitness of Christ’s majesty on the holy mountain. Prophecy came as the Holy Spirit moved men, not by human will.
chapters.2.lds: Why can promised freedom become a form of slavery when conduct remains corrupt?
chapters.2.summary: Peter warns that false teachers will come among them, as false prophets did. In greed they will exploit the readers with made-up words. God did not spare the angels who sinned or the ancient world. He saved Noah and rescued Lot from Sodom. These teachers despise authority and are like unreasoning animals. They have followed the way of Balaam, who loved the wages of wrongdoing. They are springs without water. They promise freedom, and their last state is worse than the first.
chapters.3.lds: How does patient waiting change present conduct without supplying a date for the coming day?
chapters.3.summary: Peter says this is his second letter and reminds them of the prophets’ words. Mockers will ask where the promise of his coming is. They forget that the world was once destroyed by water. The present heavens and earth are kept for fire. With the Lord one day is as a thousand years. The day of the Lord will come like a thief. They should live in holiness and look for new heavens and a new earth. Peter mentions Paul’s letters, which some twist.
